name: plate-44-carrier-v17
version_tag: #140 THREE-STATION CARRIER CHAIN — gives feb and leap their pivots (board 02h had only the month post, so 2 of the 3 v17 receivers had nowhere to mount). A post rising from the board to the feb station is impossible — it would spear the rotating month satellite (lamina r17.19 vs 4.81mm station spacing), which is exactly why the patent carries stud 218 ON stud 214. Printable form: the chain is a STACK of flat pieces like the sun tower — each is a plate + one riser, prints flat, ZERO supports. board 02j (month post extended to assy 14.0 so arm 1 can seat) + arm 1 (12.7-14.0, pressed on the month post, riser at the FEB station) + arm 2 (17.2-18.5, pressed on the feb post, riser at the LEAP station) + a 1.0mm sun spacer. ALTITUDES RESOLVED: the sun tower piece is 4.5mm, so stacking three puts the mesh bands 4.5mm apart -> satellites at assy 9.5/14.0/18.5 (was 9.5/13/16.5). That 4.5 spacing is what makes the crossover possible: 3mm satellites leave a 1.5mm gap = 1.3mm arm + 0.2mm running clearance. GATES PASS: arms clear the rotating fingers below by 0.20mm each; all three finger bands sit inside their sun slim cores; all three mesh laminae land on their sun bands. Press fits: arm bores 2.60 onto design-2.70 posts (prints 2.64) = 0.04 interference — expect to tap. 4 parts, flat, no supports, xy-comp -0.06. | QUIET.
